lesson_topic: Intellectual Property Law — The Bundle of Rights Model (Introductory Module)

principles.evidence: No non-decorative graphics, diagrams, charts, or illustrations are present across any of the five slides; all content is delivered exclusively through text blocks. The visual channel carries no informational weight independent of the verbal channel, violating the core multimedia condition.

The transcript is a verbatim replication of the on-screen text on all five slides, with no elaboration, paraphrasing, or additional information in the narration channel. On-screen text consists of full prose paragraphs rather than keywords or short phrases, and word counts exceed a five-second scan threshold on every slide.

All complex descriptions are delivered via dense on-screen prose paragraphs rather than via narration over supporting visuals, with the visual channel carrying no graphics or diagrams whatsoever. The narration adds no information beyond what is fully present in the on-screen text, making the narration channel redundant rather than complementary.

No decorative clipart, stock imagery, or extraneous visuals are present, and the narration contains no tangential anecdotes or off-topic digressions. The slide backgrounds appear clean and the content is topically focused, though the absence of any visual elements limits full coherence assessment.

No visual cues such as arrows, highlights, bold text, or color contrast are present to mark key elements, and no captions or callouts exist because there are no graphics to annotate. The narration contains no verbal signaling language directing learner attention to critical concepts, and no single most-important takeaway per slide is visually or verbally emphasized.

No labels, captions, or graphics are present on any slide, so spatial contiguity between text and visuals cannot be evaluated in the affirmative. The absence of any visual referents means the principle is structurally unachievable in this artifact as produced.
